findings.title: Incorrect boolean logic makes team-admin/owner permission check nearly always false
findings.body:
The permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`:
```
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
    (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
    (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Since a membership typically has exactly one role (MEMBER, ADMIN, or OWNER), a user can almost never satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` simultaneously. This means the variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is effectively always `false`, so team admins and owners who are not themselves the booking organizer or an attendee will be rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests, defeating the intent of granting admins/owners this permission.

findings.title: Team members never notified because evt.team is never populated
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` in email-manager.ts iterates `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify all team members with `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail`, but the `CalendarEvent` object (`evt`) constructed in `addGuestsHandler` never sets a `team` property. As a result, `calendarEvent.team` is always `undefined` for this flow, so the team-member notification loop is dead code and only the single organizer email (from `booking.userId`) ever receives the organizer notification for team-based bookings, even though other team members may need to be informed guests were added.

findings.title: No check that booking is not cancelled before adding guests
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking and performs permission checks but never verifies the booking's status (e.g. `CANCELLED`/`REJECTED`). This allows adding guests to cancelled or rejected bookings, which doesn't make logical sense and could trigger calendar/video updates and emails for events that no longer exist.

findings.title: Guest emails deduped against existing attendees but not against each other, and comparison is case-sensitive
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` is filtered only against `booking.attendees` (`!booking.attendees.some(...)`) and does not remove duplicate entries within the submitted `guests` array itself, nor normalize case. If duplicates (or case-variant duplicates, e.g. `a@b.com` vs `A@B.com`) are submitted in a single call -- which bypasses the client-side `AddGuestsDialog` uniqueness check if called directly via API -- multiple attendee rows with effectively the same email can be created via `createMany`, leading to duplicate attendee records on the booking.

findings.title: Email send failures are silently swallowed with console.log instead of being logged with context
Dead fallback branch in error toast message
No upper bound on number of guests that can be added in a single request
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no maximum length constraint. A caller could submit an arbitrarily large array of guest emails in one request, causing a large number of attendee rows to be created and a large number of emails to be queued/sent in one `addGuestsHandler` invocation, which is a potential performance/abuse concern for a mutation exposed to any authenticated attendee/organizer.

findings.title: No automated tests for the new addGuests feature
findings.body: This PR introduces a brand-new mutation (`addGuestsHandler`), a new dialog (`AddGuestsDialog`), and a new reusable form component (`MultiEmail`), none of which have accompanying unit or integration tests. Given the handler contains non-trivial permission logic (which is already buggy, see other findings) and mutates booking/attendee data plus triggers calendar updates and emails, the lack of tests is a significant gap for verifying correct behavior and preventing regressions.
